Team — forwarding Starlite's redline and Elena's note. Customer is pushing 30-day non-renewal and an unrestricted 30-day termination-for-convenience for first 12 months, which would effectively let them turn off the service quickly without compensation. Given the integration work and potential prepayment profiles, I want legal's guidance on an acceptable middle ground that keeps the deal live.

Specific asks:
1) Are we comfortable accepting 30-day non-renewal in an Order Form paired with language that: a) limits termination-for-convenience to after 12 months OR b) allows termination-for-convenience earlier but with a pro rata refund and capped migration support?
2) If we accept 30 days, what remediation/limitations do we need on the termination-for-convenience (e.g., exclude custom engineering services, cap refunds to unconsumed prepayments, 30k minimum termination fee)?
3) Draft language if possible — a short snippet we can send back to the customer this week.

Attachments: Starlite_OrderForm_v3_customer_redline.pdf

Thanks,
Priyom

Priyom / Karthik — reviewing. High-level: we can get to a commercial compromise that accepts a 30-day non-renewal window, provided we also get firm guardrails on termination-for-convenience and a limited migration/transition commitment. Comments and suggested language below.

Risks: an unrestricted 30-day termination right in the first year exposes Redwood to sunk onboarding and capacity reservation costs, and increases churn risk if the customer trials short-term then leaves. We should avoid open-ended early termination without compensation.

Suggested compromise (to propose to customer):
1) Auto-renew: Order Form will automatically renew for successive 12-month periods unless either party provides written notice of non-renewal at least 30 days prior to the end of the then-current Term.

2) Termination for Convenience (compromise):
- Either party may terminate the Order Form for convenience after the Initial Term (12 months) by providing at least 60 days' prior written notice; or
- During the Initial Term, Customer may terminate for convenience upon 30 days' prior written notice, provided that Customer pays a termination fee equal to the greater of (i) unearned prepaid Fees for the remainder of the Initial Term, or (ii) USD 25,000, and Redwood will provide reasonable migration assistance (30 days, remote) at standard professional service rates.

3) Refunds / Prepayments: Any refunds for prepayment will be calculated pro rata based on unused subscription periods, net of any migration/transition costs agreed in advance.

4) Exclusions: Termination for convenience will not apply to discrete professional services SOWs and custom engineering commitments unless expressly included in the termination calculation.

Suggested clause text (copy for the redline):
"The Order Form shall have an Initial Term of twelve (12) months. At the conclusion of the Initial Term, the Order Form shall automatically renew for additional twelve (12) month periods unless either party provides written notice of non-renewal at least thirty (30) days prior to the end of the then-current Term. Either party may terminate the Order Form for convenience after the Initial Term upon sixty (60) days' prior written notice. During the Initial Term, Customer may terminate for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice, provided that Customer pays a termination fee equal to the greater of (a) the unearned portion of any prepaid Fees for the remainder of the Initial Term, or (b) Twenty Five Thousand United States Dollars (USD 25,000). Termination for convenience shall not apply to any separately scoped professional services SOW or custom engineering commitment unless expressly stated in such SOW. Upon termination, Redwood will provide reasonable migration assistance at standard professional services rates for up to thirty (30) days."

If you want, I can convert the text into a tracked-change PDF for Priyom to send. Recommend the USD 25k floor to discourage token trials and to cover ramp costs.

LM
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference

Elena / Jordan — thanks for the quick feedback and for sharing your redline. After review with legal we've put together a compromise that we think meets procurement's need for a 30-day non-renewal window while protecting both parties from one-sided early exits.

Summary of compromise:
- Auto-renew: 30-day notice prior to end of term (we can accept).
- Termination for convenience: available during the Initial Term (12 months) with 30 days' notice but subject to either a pro rata refund or a termination fee (greater of unearned prepaid fees or USD 25,000). After the Initial Term, termination for convenience requires 60 days' notice. Redwood will provide up to 30 days of remote migration assistance at standard rates.

I've attached our redlined version with the suggested language implemented: RDW_Proposed_Term_Compromise_redline.pdf. If that's acceptable we can update the Order Form and get a DocuSign envelope out this week — hoping to keep the signature window open for the week of 11/22.

Please confirm by COB next Friday (11/19) so we can lock in pricing and start procurement flows.

Thanks,
